title: Making ten to add 8 + 5
examples: What is the make ten strategy?
How do I add 8 and 5 in my head?
What does bridging through ten mean?

explain.say: Here is 8 plus 5. Look at the ten frame. There are 8 counters. 5 more counters are coming. You will fill the frame first.
First, fill the frame. 8 needs 2 more to make 10. The 2 new counters fill the empty boxes. Now you have a full ten.
You used 2 of the 5 counters, so 3 are left. They start a new frame. Now you see 10 and 3 more. 10 and 3 make 13.
So 8 plus 5 equals 13. You split the 5 into 2 and 3. The 2 made a ten. This way of adding is called making ten. Try 9 plus 4 the same way.
Look at the board. 9 needs 1 to make 10. 3 are left from the 4. 10 and 3 make 13, so 9 plus 4 is 13. Now try 7 plus 6.

faq.q: What is the make ten strategy?
faq.a: It is a way to add by filling up a ten first. For 8 plus 5, give 2 of the 5 to the 8 to make 10, then add the 3 left: 13.

faq.q: What does bridging through ten mean?
faq.a: Bridging means crossing over, like a bridge. You go up to 10 first, then over it with what is left. 8 plus 5 goes 8, then 10, then 13.
Because 8 needs exactly 2 to make 10. Your number bonds tell you that, and 5 is 2 and 3, so 3 are left over.
asks: How do I know how to split the number?

faq.q: Does making ten work with bigger numbers?
faq.a: Yes. For 28 plus 5, 28 needs 2 to make 30, then add the other 3 to get 33. It is the same trick.
asks: Can I use it for 28 plus 5?

faq.q: How do I add 7 and 6 by making ten?
faq.a: 7 needs 3 to make 10. Split 6 into 3 and 3. Then 10 plus 3 is 13, so 7 plus 6 equals 13.

facts: Making ten is a key mental strategy in the Singapore maths curriculum.

quiz.say: You add 9 plus 6 by making ten. How do you split the 6?
quiz.why: 9 needs 1 to make 10. So split 6 into 1 and 5, and 10 and 5 make 15.

wrong.1: 9 needs only 1 to make 10, so 3 is too many.
wrong.2: 9 needs only 1 to make 10, so 2 is 1 too many.

quiz.say: Add 7 plus 5. Fill a ten first.
quiz.why: 7 needs 3 to make 10. 2 are left, and 10 and 2 make 12.

wrong.0: 11 is 1 short. Count the 2 left over again.
wrong.2: 13 is 1 too many. Only 2 are left after you make 10.
